title: A fibrewise dense affine open with Cartier boundary over a Dedekind affine
statement: Let $D$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one, put $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $p:X\to S$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. There exist an affine open subscheme $A\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and an effective Cartier divisor $E\subseteq X$ with $|E|=|X|\setminus|A|$. An effective Cartier divisor means a closed subscheme whose ideal is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal, def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. For every geometric point $\bar s$ of $S$, $A_{\bar s}$ is dense in $X_{\bar s}$ [def-pc-base-change], meaning its topological closure equals $|X_{\bar s}|$. No group action, section, connectedness, properness, or Néron mapping property is assumed. Empty fibres, $X=\varnothing$, and $E=\varnothing$ are allowed.

source.place: BLR 6.4 Lemma 4 and the construction in the proof of Theorem 1 after Lemma 4, printed pp.155–156 (PDF pp.161–162); the construction uses only smooth separated finite type of X, not its torsor structure. The Cartier boundary is the closure of the effective generic-fibre divisor used there; regularity supplies its Cartier structure. Local PDF WANTED; primary scan read online.

proof.text: Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}D$ and let $\eta=(0)\in S$. Every nonzero prime of $D$ is maximal, and its localization has dimension one: the chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ has length one, and dimension one rules out a longer chain. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] this localization is Noetherian and a normal domain. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-dim-one-iff-normal] makes it regular local. At $(0)$ the localization is the field $K$, regular of dimension zero. Thus $D$ is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

The affine scheme $S$ is Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] every nonempty set of closed subsets of $|X|$ has a minimal element, so every descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes and $|X|$ is a Noetherian topological space; and $X$ is separated by [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated]. Cover $X$ by affine opens $V$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Each restricted map $V\to S$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]; its ring map $D\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] make these rings regular. Thus $X$ is regular, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal] makes all its local rings normal domains. By [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components], $X$ is a finite disjoint union of open and closed integral regular schemes. If $X$ is empty, take $A=E=\varnothing$; below assume $X$ nonempty.

source.place: Tag 07NF (lemma-regular-goes-up), Tag 0567 (lemma-regular-normal); properties.tex Tag 0357 (lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles); BLR 6.4 Lemma 4, regularity hypotheses

proof.text:
The morphism $p$ is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Thus at $x$ over $t$ its stalk homomorphism $D_t\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Both rings are Noetherian by Steps 1--2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to this local map and the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. The quotient by the extended maximal ideal of $D_t$ is the fibre local ring by [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient]. We obtain
$$\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=\dim D_t+\dim\mathcal O_{X_t,x}.$$
At a generic point of a fibre the last dimension is zero, since it has no strictly more general point in that fibre [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains]. Thus its dimension in $X$ is zero over $\eta$ and one over a closed point. Every generic point of $X$ lies over $\eta$: its local dimension is zero by the same chain criterion, so the formula rules out every nonzero prime of $D$.

Fix a closed point $s\in S$. The closed subset $p^{-1}(s)$ has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components]; the fibre projection identifies its underlying space with this closed subset by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Take their generic points and those of $X$, using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. This is a finite set of points with Noetherian local rings of dimension at most one by Step 3. Every quasi-compact open of the Noetherian $X$ has finitely many components, again by the Noetherian finite-component theorem [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Apply [lem-trf-codimension-one-points-affine-neighbourhood] to obtain an affine open $U_s\subset X$ containing this set. It is dense in $X$ and has dense intersection with $X_s$, because it contains the generic point of every component of each of these spaces.

source.place: Tag 09NN (proposition-finite-set-of-points-of-codim-1-in-affine), substituting for BLR 6.4 Lemma 4; properties.tex Tag 0BA8

proof.text: Write $F_s=X\setminus U_s$. It has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], with generic points $\xi_{sj}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. By [lem-sfb-affine-open-boundary-codimension-one], each $\mathcal O_{X,\xi_{sj}}$ has dimension one. Classify a component as horizontal if $p(\xi_{sj})=\eta$, otherwise as vertical. A vertical component is contained in the closed fibre of $t=p(\xi_{sj})$, because the image of its closure is contained in $\overline{\{t\}}=\{t\}$. Such a $t$ cannot equal $s$: otherwise the dimension formula of Step 3 says that $\xi_{sj}$ has fibre-local dimension zero, hence is a generic point of $X_s$, contradicting its exclusion from $U_s$.

source.place: Tag 0BCV (lemma-complement-affine-open); BLR 6.4 proof of Theorem 1 after Lemma 4, removal of vertical boundary divisors

proof.text: Remove from $S$ the finitely many closed points supporting these vertical components. The remaining open contains $s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], choose a basic open $S_s=D(f_s)$ containing $s$ inside it. Set $X_s^\circ=p^{-1}(S_s)$ and $U_s^\circ=U_s\cap X_s^\circ$. This last open is affine: on the affine $U_s$ it is the principal open of the pullback of $f_s$, so use clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme]. The boundary $X_s^\circ\setminus U_s^\circ$ consists precisely of the intersections with the horizontal components of $F_s$. Each such component keeps its generic point when intersected with $X_s^\circ$, since $\eta\in S_s$. The opens $S_s$, for all closed $s$, cover $S$: they contain every closed point and each contains $\eta$. As $S$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], choose a finite subcover $S_1,\ldots,S_n$, with corresponding affine opens $U_i\subset X_i=p^{-1}(S_i)$.

source.place: 6.4 proof of Theorem 1, printed p.155, shrinking the affine base neighbourhoods and taking a finite cover; algebra.tex Tag 00E0, principal opens

proof.text:
Let $H_1,\ldots,H_r$ be the distinct closures in $X$ of the horizontal boundary components of all $X_i\setminus U_i$. Each such closure equals the original horizontal component of $F_s$ used before shrinking, since $X_i$ contains its generic point. There are finitely many, and each has its original generic point $\xi_a$ over $\eta$. Its local ring in $X$ still has dimension one: its generic point belonged to $X_i$, an open subscheme with exactly the same local ring, and Step 5 gave dimension one before shrinking. In particular no $H_a$ is a component of $X$. Put $H=\bigcup_a H_a$. Then
$$X_i\setminus U_i\subseteq H\cap X_i.$$
Indeed each boundary component on the left is one of the horizontal components whose closure was included in $H$. This is the support version of BLR's sum of generic-fibre boundary divisors and their closure; keeping each prime once suffices.

source.place: 6.4 proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.155--156: choose a divisor on the generic fibre and close its support in X

proof.text: No $H_a$ contains a component of a closed fibre. Otherwise let $z$ be the generic point of that component. By Step 3, $\dim\mathcal O_{X,z}=1$. Since $z\in H_a=\overline{\{\xi_a\}}$, $\xi_a$ generalizes $z$ and is different from it (their images in $S$ differ). The integral component $C$ of $X$ containing $\xi_a$ is closed by Step 2, so also contains $z$; its generic point $\zeta$ strictly generalizes $\xi_a$, since $H_a\ne C$. Thus $z,\xi_a,\zeta$ is a chain of length two, contradicting [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains]. No generic-fibre component is contained in $H_a$ either: at its generic point the local dimension in $X$ is zero by Step 3, ruling out a strict generalization to $\xi_a$, while equality would contradict $\dim\mathcal O_{X,\xi_a}=1$. Since $H$ is a finite union, irreducibility implies that it contains no component of any fibre. Consequently $A=X\setminus H$ is dense in every residue-field fibre.

source.place: 6.4 proof of Theorem 1, printed p.156, horizontal closure cannot contain a closed-fibre component; properties.tex Tag 02IZ gives the explicit chain argument

proof.text: Give $H_a$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is integral because its topology is irreducible and it is reduced [def-pc-integral-scheme]. It is contained in a unique integral open and closed component $C$ of $X$ from Step 2, and is closed in $C$. This $C$ is regular and locally Noetherian, with $\dim\mathcal O_{C,\xi_a}=1$. Apply [lem-per-regular-prime-divisor-local-equations] to $H_a\hookrightarrow C$: its ideal is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor. On the other open and closed components take the unit ideal. These ideals give the reduced ideal of $H_a$ in all of $X$, so $H_a\hookrightarrow X$ is an effective Cartier divisor. This also verifies the regularity hypothesis that BLR uses for the closure divisor.

source.place: Tag 0AGA (lemma-weil-divisor-is-cartier-UFD) on regular components; schemes.tex Tags 01J3 and 01J4 for reduced induced closed structures

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I_a$ be these effective Cartier ideals and put $\mathcal I=\prod_{a=1}^r\mathcal I_a$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. The product is quasi-coherent and defines a closed subscheme $E$ with support $H$, by repeated application of [lem-weil-pbc-product-ideal-closed-subscheme-union]. To verify its Cartier property explicitly, at a point choose affine neighbourhoods on which each $\mathcal I_a$ has a regular generator. Repeated use of [lem-sc-affine-inter-principal-both] gives a common affine neighbourhood principal in each of them. Restriction is localization by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme](0); an injective multiplication map stays injective after localization (if $fu/g^m=0$, some $g^kfu=0$, so $g^ku=0$). Thus all restricted generators are non-zero-divisors on the common neighbourhood. Their product is a non-zero-divisor and generates $\mathcal I$ there. This is [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. For $r=0$ take $\mathcal I=\mathcal O_X$, giving $E=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0AGA and the finite-sum construction in Tag 0BCW (lemma-complement-open-affine-effective-cartier-divisor); coherent.tex Tag 0CYV, product ideal support

proof.text: For every $i$ put $A_i=A\cap X_i$. Step 7 implies $A_i\subseteq U_i$, and $A_i$ is the open complement in the affine $U_i$ of $E|_{U_i}$. The inclusion $A_i\hookrightarrow U_i$ is affine: cover $U_i$ by affine opens on which $\mathcal I$ has a single regular generator $h$; its inverse image is the principal affine open $D(h)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme](0), and apply the target-local criterion [pqf-lem-affine-local-target]. Since $U_i$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](2) shows $A_i$ affine. Apply [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] again to $A\to S$ and the affine cover $\{S_i\}$: its inverse images are exactly $A_i$ (open pullbacks [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product]). Hence $A\to S$ is affine, and $S$ affine implies $A$ affine by the same permanence lemma. This proves the affineness assertion of BLR's gluing construction without assuming that an arbitrary open of an affine scheme is affine.

source.place: Tag 07ZU (lemma-complement-effective-Cartier-divisor), affine-local proof; morphisms.tex Tags 01S8 (lemma-characterize-affine), 01SG (lemma-affine-permanence); BLR 6.4 proof of Theorem 1, printed p.156

proof.text: We have constructed the affine open $A=X\setminus H$ and an effective Cartier divisor $E$ with $|E|=H$. By Step 8 the open $A$ is dense in every residue-field fibre of the smooth $X\to S$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-fibrewise-dense-open-base-change] to each morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ defining a geometric point, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. It gives density of $A_{\bar s}$ in $X_{\bar s}$, including empty fibres. The empty boundary and empty total scheme have already been included in Steps 2 and 10. No step used a group action, a section, properness, or connectedness of $X$.

source.place: 2.5, S-density and Lemma 1(b), printed pp.55--56, base-change stability; 6.4 proof of Theorem 1, conclusion of the fibrewise dense affine construction
